name: normalization
description: Cross-SDK matching-time normalization (§6). Each case pins the exact output of normalizeForMatching / normalize_for_matching (NFKC + zero-width strip + curated confusable fold) for a given input. Both SDK harnesses (sdk-typescript/tests/unit/normalization.test.ts, sdk-python/tests/test_normalization.py) feed every `input` through their normalizer and must produce the pinned `normalized` string byte-for-byte. `matches_override` additionally pins that a keyword rule for "override" fires on the normalized copy while the raw input would have dodged it. A divergence is a release blocker unless recorded in conformance/known-divergences.md. This is a MATCHING-only transform: it never mutates stored/forwarded content.

cases.note: Plain ASCII is unchanged — normalization never perturbs existing behavior.
U+200D ZERO WIDTH JOINER spliced into the keyword is stripped.
ZWSP, soft hyphen, BOM, word joiner all stripped.
Fullwidth Latin letters fold to ASCII under NFKC.
Cyrillic small o (U+043E) folds to Latin o; NFKC alone would not.
Greek small omicron (U+03BF) folds to Latin o.
Confusable + zero-width combined still collapses to the keyword.
Bidirectional format controls (LRM/RLM, embeddings/overrides, isolates) are invisible and must be stripped before matching.
Non-confusable characters (incl. astral/emoji) pass through unchanged.
No keyword present after normalization — must not falsely match.

Unicode 16 Outlined Latin (U+1CCD6..U+1CCEF). Node's ICU NFKC folds these to ASCII and CPython's frozen unicodedata does not, so a keyword rule BLOCKED in TypeScript and ALLOWED in Python until the curated fold covered them. Pinned here because the divergence is a function of the HOST's Unicode version, which no test running on one runtime can see.

Outlined digits (U+1CCF0..U+1CCF9) fold to 0-9. Same host-version divergence as the letters; separate because a PII pattern is digits, so the letters alone would have left the card/SSN case uncovered.

U+A7F1 was assigned in Unicode 17.0, so ICU folds it to 'S' and no shipping CPython does. It sits in a DIFFERENT block from the outlined letters, which is why counting the residue as 'the Outlined Latin block' undercounts it.
